_comment: Success-score component weights, per position. Goal contributions (perf_level/perf_delta) are a weak-to-meaningless signal for defenders/goalkeepers (most keepers have 0 goals+assists both before and after a move), so their weight is shifted toward value growth, playing time, value for money, and defensive_technical instead. defensive_technical (rating/defensive actions/passing for outfielders, rating/saves/save%/goals-conceded for goalkeepers - see compute_defensive_technical_pct in build_dataset.py) is only known for the ~85% of transfers with FotMob tenure stats (data/raw/fotmob_stats_cache.csv, built by scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py - optional, like the resale/loan cache below) - for the rest its weight is dropped and the other weights renormalized, same pattern as resale_profit. resale_profit's weight is NOT the flat number below - it varies by tenure length per resale_weight_curve (a quick flip weights resale heavily since that's often the point of the deal; a long career barely moves regardless of the eventual sale price, since the club already extracted years of value). The number here is just the weight at the curve's ~2-year reference point, kept for documentation. Only known for the ~17% of transfers where the club actually resold the player for a recorded fee - for the rest it's excluded and the other weights are renormalized to sum to 1 (see build_dataset.py). Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row (including resale_profit) must sum to 1.0.

resale_weight_curve._comment: resale_weight(tenure_years) = min + (max - min) * exp(-tenure_years / decay_years). A few months' tenure -> ~18-20% weight; ~2 years -> ~8.6% (close to the old flat 8%); 6+ years -> under 3%.
